briefs.label: Dungeon as a piece palette plus placement rows
briefs.why: A dungeon is a short list of piece names and a list of placements. Empty zones show as zero rows and fail a coverage check. The data is the zone; the look is a palette.
keep: placement rows (index, position, angle, and a second row type for props)
zero rows flagged as an empty zone
change: our arenas are rings with our own pieces, not corridors
placement rows also carry a hit radius and a telegraph flag
no reuse of the donor's piece names or layouts

briefs.label: Translucent blood pool (flat, drawn last)
briefs.why: A flat translucent surface drawn after the floor and entities, with depth writes off, keeps the floor visible under a pool and avoids z-fighting. It fits a blood or wet-floor decal.
keep: drawn last, after floor and entities
one flat surface with the same vertex layout as the floor
change: a darker rim and a slow ripple from the hit point, in our blood colour
a fade-out over 6 s instead of staying put
a shape from a small set of pool outlines, not a full plane

briefs.label: Soft spark for hit impact (camera-facing, additive)
briefs.why: A camera-facing quad with a soft texture and additive blend reads as light and energy, and it is cheaper than geometry. It suits a hit spark.
keep: camera-facing quad built on the CPU
a placeholder texture until final art
change: a shard-shaped two-frame flash in an ember colour
tied to the impact sound on the same frame
a different spark count per hit weight

briefs.label: One creature shape, many skins (resolved by table)
briefs.why: A creature id resolves to a shape and then to a separate skin row, so one shape can carry many skins. A family reads as one monster with variants.
keep: catalogue row points to a shape and a separate skin
no texture inside the shape file
change: each family keeps its own silhouette cue (horns or crest) so skins never read as the same monster
skin palettes chosen from our own ramps
no donor shape or skin names

briefs.label: Terrain flatten patch (arena floor by radius and falloff)
briefs.why: Each patch flattens the ground to a target height inside a radius, with a falloff band, so an arena floor can be set from data.
keep: patch row with centre, radius, target height, falloff band
change: our own falloff curve with a flat core for duels
no region tag; one arena per patch set
patches generated by zone rules, not by hand
briefs.ref: /mnt/frankendom-donors/latentcollapse-RustDAoC/data/terrain_flatten.tsv lines 1-2 (header and first row; coordinates not copied)

inspiration: Palette fold: the CPU streams posed bones once and a compute pass multiplies each part's inverse-bind into one palette the vertex shader reads (palette_fold.wgsl lines 1-3). Header caveat: holds only for uniform scale (lines 6-8). Useful as a skinning cost idea for many creatures on a phone.
Three-table creature resolution: model id to catalogue row to shape file, with the skin in a separate table (monsters.rs lines 1-19). Our catalogue row can carry a shape id and a skin id separately.
Translucent water drawn last with depth writes off (water.wgsl lines 1-2): the floor stays visible under pools.
Soft additive billboards for effects, written as an honest placeholder (particle_billboard.wgsl lines 1-2): effects read as light, not as opaque cubes.
Dungeon as a palette of pieces plus placement rows, with zero rows counted as empty (dungeon.rs lines 1-12): zone-as-data plus a coverage check, which matches our zone-population rows.
Terrain flatten patches with a falloff band (terrain_flatten.tsv line 1 header): arena floors set by data.
Deterministic state boundary between world state and renderer, UI, audio (README line 50): matches our rule that camera, HUD and sound stay client-only.
Client-tables approach (data/client_tables): the donor keeps extracted tables with a provenance header (key_names.tsv lines 1-3). A good habit to copy with originals, not with retail data.
